title: Noor and the Kitchen
premise: Noor Haddad, a food writer grieving her grandmother's shuttered restaurant, discovers the old orchard deed lists a second name: Silas Underhill, the vineyard owner whose family debts forced her grandmother out decades ago. Neither will sell to the developer circling the land, but neither can prove sole ownership, so they must share one harvest season under one roof. As they cook, argue, and dig through buried ledgers, Noor uncovers proof that Silas's father forged the co-ownership clause to protect her grandmother from ruin — a truth that could save the orchard or destroy both families' names. In the end, they choose truth over inheritance, filing the evidence and planting a joint press of preserves called Kitchen & Vine, together.
about_author: Jude Montrose is the pen name of a former line cook who traded twelve years of kitchen shifts for quiet mornings at a writing desk in upstate New York. Their novels braise romance slowly, favoring inherited recipes, stubborn land, and love that arrives after closing time.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Clearing her late grandmother's estate, Noor finds the orchard deed bearing an impossible second name — Silas Underhill — and drives to his vineyard to confront him. He is cold, drowning in debt, and just as shocked. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into righteous anger as two strangers realize their families' histories are entangled.

chapters.title: One Roof, One Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A developer's offer forces them into an uneasy truce: share the farmhouse until the season ends, then split the sale. Shared meals thaw old resentments; Silas teaches her the vines, she revives the kitchen. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness growing in the cracks of mutual stubbornness.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Digging for documents to void Noor's claim, Silas instead finds his father's ledger: the co-ownership was forged deliberately, a shield to keep her grandmother solvent when banks came calling. Telling the truth means confessing his family built its name on a lie. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead colliding with love for the living.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The developer returns with a final deadline; Noor, having found the ledger herself, waits to see if Silas will lie to save his vineyard. At the station, he hands her the truth instead of the ticket out. They file the evidence, refuse the sale, and open the orchard's first joint harvest. Emotional beat: justice chosen over inheritance, and love allowed past tense no longer.
